hints.title: Subtree Equality Invariant
hints.text: A tree node is good if all immediate child subtrees have identical total node counts. Leaf nodes have zero subtrees and are always good.

hints.title: Bottom-Up Size Propagation
hints.text: A depth-first traversal naturally returns the size of each subtree while visiting children.

hints.title: Child Size Uniformity Check
hints.text: Compare subtree sizes across all children of the current node. If all returned sizes match, increment the good node counter.

hints.title: Reference Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countGoodNodes(self, edges: list[list[int]]) -> int:
        n = len(edges) + 1
        adj = [[] for _ in range(n)]
        for u, v in edges:
            adj[u].append(v)
            adj[v].append(u)
            
        good_count = 0
        def dfs(u, p):
            nonlocal good_count
            sub_sizes = []
            total_size = 1
            for v in adj[u]:
                if v == p:
                    continue
                sz = dfs(v, u)
                sub_sizes.append(sz)
                total_size += sz
            if len(set(sub_sizes)) <= 1:
                good_count += 1
            return total_size
            
        dfs(0, -1)
        return good_count
```

variables: n: number of nodes in the tree
complexity.notes: Single depth-first traversal over all n nodes.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Recomputing subtree sizes separately for each node takes quadratic O(n^2) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: O(n) recursion stack and adjacency list.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Computes subtree sizes recursively in post-order and checks child size uniformity.
